evidence.note: Chose tree-sitter-java as the parser layer — a foundational reuse decision that de-risks the riskiest grammar work upfront rather than hand-building lexer/parser.
Sustained understand-before-build phase: studied golden response shapes per LSP method and recorded them in golden-semantics.md before writing implementation, establishing per-layer knowledge.

Layered file creation in dependency order: main.rs (stdio/protocol) → model.rs (AST) → symbols.rs (symbol table) → resolve.rs → requests/refs/callh (per-method handlers) — the explicit layer hierarchy the anchor describes.
First integration milestone: build, fix errors, run full harness — concrete done-check that the plumbing minimally works before method work.

Method-by-method attack (references, implementation, documentSymbol, codeLens, folding, highlight, typeDefinition, hover, callHierarchy, semanticTokens), each closed by a per-method test and a recurring 'Full suite' done-check; refs+highlight batched together on shared machinery.
Repeated 'failing files ranked' passes to redirect effort toward highest-value remaining failures — revisiting the plan as pass counts reveal where value concentrates.

reasoning: Behavior clearly matches the level-8 anchor: an explicit layer hierarchy (protocol → tree-sitter parse → symbol model → per-method handlers), a prioritized method-by-method sequence where each method has a concrete test-plus-full-suite done-check, and later methods build on validated shared machinery (refs/highlight batched). Several level-10 traits appear — reuse to de-risk grammar early, method-group batching, and late reprioritization by failing-file ranking — but the method sequence was not cleanly cost-to-pass ordered (references, the hardest, was ground on very early) and there is no visible explicit spike/milestone-declaration prose, keeping it at 8 rather than higher.
